what: switching power, energy and clock predicted per (format, kind) BEFORE E78 (aifoundry3, 600 MHz pinned) and E80 (aifoundry2, its own governor) run.  No card was touched; nothing here is a measurement.
basis: every switching W is over that TYPE's OWN zero-data level (E67's `anchor_zeros`: a running kernel on zero operands), at 600 MHz and 521.8 mV on aifoundry3

kinds_spec.revision: 2 (Sat 31 Oct 2026, after verification: int8's stream and gate corrected from the TIMA path, the two value-sort baselines committed, replicate bands added, tier counts fixed)

gating_arm.selected_on: E64's fp32 sparse75, the only measured kind that is mostly gated
gating_arm.what_the_arms_are: `bus`: a gated column-slot-cycle still pays its operand-bus flips.  `gate`: it pays none of them (vpu_lane.v clock-gates the lane, so its input registers do not capture).  E78's sparse kinds settle it.

anchored_on.wa_inf: E70 nrd_a 7.209 +- 0.015 W (random A, constant B)
anchored_on.wb_inf: E70 nrd_b 10.785 +- 0.024 W (constant A, random B)
anchored_on.sigma: E64's fp32 `signs` (+-1.0f), 13.10 W over zeros, carried to a3's voltage
anchored_on.lam: DECLARED ZERO: a fitted overlap came out at -0.029, zero to within 3%
anchored_on.u: E67/E70 anchors: a running kernel on zero data against one on a constant nonzero

e70_fit_for_comparison.note: E70's own fits, which its own top rungs EXCEED (nrd_a 7.209 > 6.37, nrd_b 10.785 > 10.52) and whose A-side FORM E70 rejects; they are the sensitivity arm, not the primary

fp32.sign_term_reading: sigma = 8.16 W is what a product-sign change costs when it happens on every one of the 4,096 column-slot-cycles.  The operand-bus price of the sign bit itself is 0.56 W a position (E65 bit 31) -- 15x less.  This is the term no per-position price list can carry, because E65 and E67 measured every mask against a CONSTANT other operand.

fp32_out_of_sample.what: the model, with its four fp32 numbers fixed, against E64's measured kinds it was NOT fitted on.  a_randn_b_ones and a_ones_b_randn are the card-transfer check: E70's one-sided random-operand steps measured on aifoundry3 against E64's measured on aifoundry2.

fp16.u_from: E64 (c_ones - c_zeros) x 1.01865, ONE run each
fp16.alpha_reading: alpha = 1 would mean the significand-width scaling r_T is exactly right; this is a prediction E79's own fp16/int8 price lists can falsify

int8.u_from: E64 (c_ones - c_zeros) x 1.01865, ONE run each
int8.alpha_reading: alpha = 1 would mean the significand-width scaling r_T is exactly right; this is a prediction E79's own fp16/int8 price lists can falsify

alt_gating_arm.what: the whole model re-calibrated under the other reading of the gate, carried per kind as `switching_w_alt_gating_arm`.  The kinds where the two arms disagree most are exactly the ones E78 should run first: they settle whether a clock-gated lane still pays its operand bus.

u_per_format.reading: int8's lane un-gating term is 0.57 W against fp32's 8.555 -- 15x smaller.  int8 runs on TIMA with the txfma clock OFF (vpu_tensorfma.v:157-166, 626-628), so most of what fp32 pays merely to have a live lane is not switched on at all.  It rests on ONE E64 run per point, so its interval is +-1.19 W.

kinds_json_reproduced.what: sha256 of all 51 tiles, plus this file's own stream, gate and bus counts against kinds.json's stats.bus_bits_per_op and stats.gated_lane_frac for every kind

e70_additive_sums.what: E70's own additive sums S for its nine lq and seven alq rungs, re-derived from this file's E65/E67 price lists position by position.  The residual is the 2 dp rounding of the published lists.  E70's seven spread (ls) rungs use a mask its item table defines and are not re-derived here.

simulate_port.what: this file's copy of E64's governor against the import, on E64's own fp32 randn powers

speed_on_e64_own_c.what: the same two simulations on E64's OWN fitted c, against its measured SUS clocks

fp32/a_randn_b_zeros.rule: A randn, B all +0.0: every accumulate lane gated by the B side

fp32/a_zeros_b_randn.rule: A all +0.0, B randn: gated by the A side, which is the broadcast one

fp32/bf16trunc.rule: randn with the low 16 mantissa bits zeroed: bf16 precision in an fp32 word

fp32/fp16grid.rule: randn rounded to the nearest fp16 value: the low 13 mantissa bits zeroed

fp32/neg_ones.rule: every element -1.0 (0xBF800000): `ones` with the sign bit set

fp32/nn_like.rule: A = relu(randn) activations (half exactly +0.0), B = 0.02*randn weights

fp32/pow2.rule: 2^(U{0..16} - 8), the host's `pow2`: mantissa 0, exponent random, sign 0

fp32/randn_large.rule: normal, sigma 2^10: the same mantissas, an exponent band 10 higher

fp32/randn_small.rule: normal, sigma 2^-10: the same mantissas, an exponent band 10 lower

fp32/randn_sorted.rule: `randn`'s own 512 words, permuted into the unit's stream order of least change

fp32/smallint.rule: integers -8..7 drawn uniformly, as floats: the int4 range, 1/16 of them zero

fp32/sparse50.rule: randn with half the elements (= words, E=1) set to +0.0

fp32/sparse90.rule: randn with 90% of the elements set to +0.0

fp32/uniform01.rule: uniform [0, 1): sign always 0, exponent always below 127

fp32/zeros.rule: every element +0.0 (0x00000000): every lane gated on an accumulate pass

fp16/a_zeros_b_randn.rule: A all zero, B randn: the other orientation, the broadcast side gated

fp16/fp8grid.rule: randn rounded to the nearest e4m3 value, held in fp16: 3 mantissa bits

fp16/nn_like.rule: A = relu(randn), B = 0.02*randn, both in fp16

fp16/pair_half_zero.rule: in every (a1, a2) pair exactly one half is zero: the word never gates, but PRM 9.4's two-term update is dropped on every one of the 4,096 updates

fp16/randn.rule: standard normal, sigma 1, rounded to fp16

fp16/randn_small.rule: normal, sigma 2^-6, rounded to fp16: fp16's exponent range is only 5 bits

fp16/randn_sorted.rule: `randn`'s own words, permuted into the stream order of least change

fp16/sparse50.rule: randn with half the ELEMENTS zero: only 1/4 of the words gate

fp16/sparse90.rule: randn with 90% of the elements zero: 81% of the words gate

fp16/wsparse50.rule: randn with half the WORDS zero: the kind that really gates half of fp16's lanes

fp16/wsparse90.rule: randn with 90% of the words zero

int8/a_zeros_b_full.rule: A all zero, B uniform -128..127: the broadcast side gated instead

int8/full.rule: uniform over -128..127, the whole two's-complement range (E64's int8 `randn`)

int8/gauss_q.rule: round(16*randn) clipped to +-127: a quantised weight, most bytes small

int8/highbit.rule: +64 or -64 (0x40 / 0xC0): one magnitude bit, the sign changing

int8/neg_ones.rule: every byte -1 (0xFF), word 0xFFFFFFFF: every bit set

int8/pos.rule: uniform over 0..127, sign bit always 0 (E64's int8 `uniform`)

int8/smallint.rule: uniform over -8..7: the int4 range inside an int8 byte

int8/sorted.rule: `full`'s own words, permuted into the stream order of least change

int8/sparse50.rule: `full` with half the BYTES zero: only 1/16 of the words gate

int8/sparse90.rule: `full` with 90% of the bytes zero: 65.6% of the words gate

int8/ternary.rule: -1, 0, +1 with equal probability: a ternary-quantised weight

int8/wsparse50.rule: `full` with half the WORDS zero: still gates only ~5/8 of int8's lanes, because the gate wants BOTH words of the column pair

model.burst: surface_hpl.py simulate, tau 1.3 s, pass 0.24 s, 65 W, cool die, mean clock 4-12 s on p_f = E64's B_f + c*s_f
model.sustained: surface_hpl_t.py at gamma 3.0, die a state on E64's thermal line, tau_th 14 s, thermal limb trip 66 C, mean clock 40-80 s

interval_rule.what: 1 sigma is the quadrature of: (i) a relative band on the (operand bits + product sign) terms, zero for a calibration kind, 12% for an out-of-sample fp32 kind (its own measured out-of-sample median miss is 6%, max 34% on the smallest value) and 30% for fp16/int8, whose whole price list is one fitted scalar; (ii) E70's law fit rms 0.232 W times the live fraction; (iii) U's error times the live fraction; (iv) the calibration TARGET's own error (fp32 the split's 0.37 W; fp16/int8 E64's single-run 1.19 W), pro-rated by size; (v) the gate rate's single-tile sd from kinds.json times U.  ci95 is 2 sigma.  It does NOT cover the two structural unknowns: the A-side broadcast weight, and int8's provisional stream.

decision_rules.R1: E78: the measured switching power over the type's own zeros level is inside `switching_w_ci95` for at least 70% of the fp32 kinds run, and at least 50% of the fp16 and int8 kinds.
decision_rules.R2: E78: the ORDER is right -- Spearman correlation of predicted against measured switching power >= 0.90 within each format, over every kind run.
decision_rules.R3: E78: the gate's signature.  (sparse50 - wsparse50) switching power is >= 2 W in BOTH fp16 and int8 (wsparse50 gates more, so it must cost less), and |fp32 sparse50 - fp32 wsparse50| <= 1.0 W, because in fp32 element sparsity IS word sparsity and the two are one kind.
decision_rules.R4: E78: int8 (ones - zeros) switching power <= 2.0 W, against fp32's 8.555 W.  This is the sharpest structural prediction in this file and the one most likely to fail, because it rests on a single E64 run per point (+- 1.19 W).
decision_rules.R5: E79: alpha_fp16 and alpha_int8 land in [0.5, 2.0] when re-solved against E79's own measured fp16/int8 per-bit prices -- i.e. the significand-width scaling is right to a factor of two.
decision_rules.R6: E78: the product-sign term is real.  fp32 `neg_ones` costs within 1 W of `ones` (no sign CHANGE: every element is -1.0, so the product's sign never moves), while int8 `ternary` and `highbit`, whose signs do change, cost at least 1 W more than int8 `ones`.
decision_rules.R9: E78: the gate's reach.  fp32 `a_randn_b_zeros` is 100% gated by the B side while its A operand bus keeps moving (27,920 bits an op).  The `gate` arm says it costs ~0 W over zeros; the `bus` arm says it costs several watts.  Whichever E78 measures SELECTS the arm, and every kind's `switching_w_alt_gating_arm` is this file's prediction under the other one.  This is the single most informative cell in the matrix and E78 should run it first.
decision_rules.R7: E80: predicted burst MHz within 25 MHz of measured for at least 70% of the cells run, and every cell predicted at 800 MHz measures >= 790 MHz.
decision_rules.R8: E80: the sustained LIMIT is called right (thermal vs power) for every cell, and the predicted sustained MHz is within 40 MHz of measured for at least 70% of them.

departures: E64's own tiles were never dumped, so the fp32 scoring tiles for its ten host kinds are STAND-INS drawn from the host's own rules (main.cpp:458-478) with numpy, not libstdc++'s distributions.  Each row carries its draw sd over 24 draws.

The law's curvature is anchored on E70's measured nrd_a / nrd_b rather than on E70's own fitted W-infinity, because E70's own top rungs and those two measurements both sit ABOVE its fit and it warns that the fit is not a ceiling.  E70's 6.37 / 10.52 W are the sensitivity arm.

E70 REJECTS the saturating FORM on the A side (its increments accelerate).  The A arm is declared, not selected.  rho = 1.246 is the alternative pricing and the x8 / x16 broadcast multiplier is a counting convention, not a measurement: E78 must validate the A-side weight.
The product-sign term is NEW here.  It makes E64's fp32 `signs` a calibration kind, so fp32 now has four fitted numbers (WA, WB, lam, sigma) against six out-of-sample measured kinds.

int8's bus and Hamming figures are PROVISIONAL in kinds.json (they rest on the reconstructed 256-micro-op / 16-slot TIMA stream), so every int8 switching prediction here is provisional with them.  Its gated_* figures are not.
gamma = 3.0 is this lane's declared choice among E64-T1's arms, on its out-of-sample sustained rms and E64's own within-run busy slope (3.12).  It is not a figure E64-T1 itself registers.

The sustained predictions inherit E69's FAILED drift check: the same cell read 49.38 W at 65.4 C on 23 Oct and 51.89 W at 65.2 C on 27 Oct, +2.51 W at one die temperature, more than the clamp band's whole 2.13 W width.  A sustained miss of that size is a thermal-path drift, not a model failure; E80 should re-read the die line before scoring R8.
